data.name: Pungenin
data.description: Phenolic glucoside from Picea wilsonii that promotes hair regrowth via transcriptional regulation of the PI3K/AKT/FoxO/mTOR axis.
data.description_beginner: A plant compound from a spruce tree, reported in lab studies to encourage hair regrowth. It appears to work by switching on the PI3K/AKT growth pathway that feeds into mTOR, telling hair-follicle cells it is time to grow again.

studies.title: Pungenin Promotes Hair Growth in Mouse Models of Androgenic Alopecia Through Transcriptional Regulation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR Axis.
studies.authors: Zhai W; Yang J; Zhang L et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse (DHT-induced AGA); primary mouse hair follicle cells
studies.finding: Topical pungenin accelerated hair regrowth in DHT-induced androgenetic alopecia mice, reducing type II 5α-reductase expression and modulating PI3K/AKT/FoxO/mTOR transcriptional signalling in hair follicle cells.
